property_summary: The sum of all account balances plus the contract's own balance must never exceed the total Ether ever sent in via Put (which is the contract's balance plus total accumulated balances). Without the overflow check, a large msg.value can overflow acc.balance on addition, making acc.balance less than the actual Ether contributed, breaking the invariant that acc.balance accurately reflects the user's contributed amount.

For any account, the recorded balance in acc.balance is always exactly equal to the sum of Ether sent via Put and fallback by that account, minus successful Collect amounts. The bug removes the overflow check, allowing acc.balance to overflow and become less than the actual Ether contributed, violating the invariant that acc.balance is at least as large as the Ether sent.

After a Put, the sender's balance is at least the Ether they just sent, because the reference checks for overflow; the bug omits the check, letting acc.balance become less than msg.value through overflow.
After any Put, the sender's balance recorded in Acc is always strictly greater than zero when they send a non-zero msg.value, but the overflow bug can cause it to wrap to zero.

For any account and any non-zero msg.value sent via Put, the recorded balance must be at least msg.value; the bug removes the overflow check, allowing the balance to wrap to a value less than msg.value.

After any sequence of calls to Put, the unlock time recorded for a sender must be strictly greater than block.timestamp at the time of the call, or at least equal to block.timestamp if _unlockTime is 0; the buggy version always leaves it as 0, making it always less than any future block.timestamp and thus allowing premature Collect.

For any account that made a Put call, the stored unlockTime must equal the maximum of the passed _unlockTime and the call's block.timestamp; the buggy version leaves it uninitialized (zero), violating this invariant.

For any account that has ever called Put, the stored unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp of that Put call; the buggy version leaves unlockTime uninitialized (zero), which is less than any non-zero block.timestamp.

For any account that has deposited via Put, the balance of that account must be non-drainable via Collect before the unlock time has passed; the buggy version allows immediate Collect because unlockTime defaults to 0, making block.timestamp > unlockTime always true.

After a Put call, the recorded unlockTime for msg.sender must equal the passed _unlockTime if it is greater than block.timestamp, otherwise block.timestamp; the buggy version leaves unlockTime at the struct's default (zero), breaking this equality for any non-zero _unlockTime.
After a Put call, the balance of the caller in Acc mapping equals the msg.value sent; the mutant fails this because it comments out the balance increment.

After a Put call, the contract's ETH balance must equal the sum of all Acc balances; the mutant fails this because it omits the balance increment, so the contract receives ETH that is not reflected in the stored balance.
For any call to Put, the sum of Acc balances across all addresses ever used in Put equals address(c).balance; the bug violates this because msg.value is received but not added to acc.balance.

After any sequence of Put calls, for any two distinct actors, the sum of their Acc balances before and after calling Collect must satisfy that a successful Collect reduces each balance by exactly the amount collected; the bug violates this because the balance is never incremented in Put, so Collect can underflow a zero balance and still succeed without actually transferring funds.
After a successful Put call, the contract's ETH balance must equal the sum of all Acc balances, and the mutant breaks this by receiving ETH without incrementing acc.balance.
Collect fails before unlock time even when balance and amount conditions are met.
Collect reverts when block.timestamp is at most the unlock time even if balance and amount conditions hold.
Collect reverts when called with amount greater than zero if the caller's unlock time is in the future, even if balance and MinSum conditions are satisfied.
Collect always reverts when called after Put with the same amount and a future unlock time
Collect must revert when called with a positive amount after Put with a future unlock time, regardless of balance.

After any sequence of Collect calls, the sum of all withdrawals by an address cannot exceed its prior balance minus MinSum unless unlock time has passed; the buggy version allows withdrawals below MinSum to succeed even when the unlock time has not passed.
For any caller, a successful Collect call requires that block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime; the buggy version allows Collect to succeed when block.timestamp <= acc.unlockTime.

For any caller, after a Collect that decreases the balance, if the calling transaction's block.timestamp is less than or equal to the caller's unlockTime, the call must revert; the mutant allows success, so a try/catch around Collect will show success when block.timestamp <= unlockTime.

For any caller with balance ≥ MinSum, if Collect succeeds when block.timestamp ≤ unlockTime then the returned balance must be unchanged (no withdrawal); the buggy version allows withdrawal, reducing balance.

For any caller, after a successful Collect(_am) that reduces the caller's balance, the block.timestamp must be strictly greater than the caller's unlockTime; the mutant allows a balance-reducing Collect to succeed when block.timestamp <= unlockTime.
Accumulated balance after a successful collect must reflect the withdrawn amount.

property_summary: A Collect call must never succeed when the account balance is below MinSum; the bug allows collection below MinSum.

After any call to Collect that succeeds, the caller's balance must remain at least MinSum unless it was already below MinSum; the mutant allows successful collection that reduces the balance below MinSum.
For any successful Collect, the caller's new balance must be either 0 or at least MinSum; the bug allows a collection that leaves the balance strictly between 0 and MinSum.

For any successful Collect, the balance before the call must not be both below MinSum and the amount _am ≤ 0; the bug allows successful collection when balance < MinSum violating the original minimum guard.
A successful Collect must not decrease the contract's Ether balance by more than the collected amount.
A successful Collect reduces the holder's Acc.balance by exactly the requested amount.
If Collect succeeds, the contract's ether balance must have decreased at most by the collected amount.
A Collect call after a Put must not succeed if the amount to collect exceeds the contract's current ether balance.
A call to Collect after a Put must revert.
For any sender and value, after Put, the sender's Acc balance and the contract's ETH balance are equal, but the overflow bug allows a wrap-around where Acc balance exceeds the contract's ETH balance.

After any number of Put calls, a holder's Acc balance never exceeds the total msg.value they have ever supplied; the missing overflow check allows wrapping so a single Put with max uint value makes the balance nearly zero while total supplied is huge.

For any sender and any sequence of payable Put calls with arbitrary msg.value and unlockTime, the sender's Acc balance never exceeds the sum of all msg.value they have ever sent; the missing overflow check allows a single Put with sufficiently large msg.value to wrap around, making the balance less than the total sent.

For any sender and any number of Put calls, the sender's Acc balance plus the contract's ETH balance after a partial Collect withdrawal is at least the total ETH deposited by that sender; the missing overflow check causes a deposit to wrap the Acc balance below the deposited amount, violating the invariant after withdrawal.

After a Put call, the accumulated balance in the Acc mapping for the caller must be at least the sum of all values previously sent via Put by that caller. The buggy version loses previous deposits by overwriting the balance instead of adding, violating this invariant.

For any caller, after two consecutive Put calls with positive values, the balance in the Acc mapping must be the sum of both values; the mutant replaces rather than adds, so the balance equals only the second value.

After any call to Put with msg.value > 0, the caller's accumulated balance (Acc[caller].balance) must be at least the amount sent in that single call; the mutant assigns msg.value instead of adding, so if there was a prior non-zero balance, the balance after the call can be strictly less than the amount just sent, violating the invariant that Acc[caller].balance >= msg.value.

For any caller that makes multiple `Put` calls where the cumulative value does not overflow, the final `Acc[caller].balance` must equal the sum of all `msg.value` sent; the mutant sets the balance to only the last `msg.value`, breaking this invariant.

After any number of Put calls by a caller, the caller's balance in Acc must equal the sum of all msg.value sent by that caller; the mutant resets balance to only the last msg.value, breaking this invariant.

In the reference contract, after calling Put with any unlockTime, the holder's unlockTime equals max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the buggy version always sets it to block.timestamp, violating this equality for inputs where _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

After any single Put call, the state variable unlockTime for the caller must be at least as large as the _unlockTime argument if _unlockTime is in the future; the buggy version sets it only to block.timestamp, which is smaller when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

After a successful Put call, if the caller's new unlockTime is in the future, it should equal max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the buggy version sets it to block.timestamp, which is smaller when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

After any single call to Put with an unlockTime in the future, the caller's unlockTime must be strictly greater than the current block.timestamp; the buggy version sets it to block.timestamp, which is not greater.

After any pair of Put calls where the second call's _unlockTime is between the first call's unlockTime and the second call's block.timestamp, the unlockTime should never decrease; the bug restamps unlockTime to block.timestamp on every Put, so a later call with a large gap can lower it.
After any call to Put, the unlockTime should be at least block.timestamp; the buggy version allows unlockTime to be less than block.timestamp.

After any call to Put, the resulting unlockTime for the caller must be greater than or equal to block.timestamp at the moment of the call; the buggy version violates this by setting unlockTime to a past _unlockTime argument.

After a Put call, if the provided _unlockTime is less than the current block.timestamp, the reference C sets unlockTime to block.timestamp, while the buggy version sets it to the past _unlockTime, making a subsequent Collect callable earlier than allowed (i.e., the reference requires block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime to collect, so a past unlockTime enables immediate collection, violating the intended time-lock invariant).

For any Put call, if the supplied _unlockTime is in the past relative to block.timestamp of the Collect attempt, a subsequent Collect call for an amount <= balance and >= MinSum should succeed only when block.timestamp > the stored unlockTime; the bug makes it succeed too early by storing the past _unlockTime directly.

For any Put call followed by a Collect call with amount _am <= balance and >= MinSum, the reference ensures that if _unlockTime was in the past, the stored unlockTime becomes block.timestamp, so Collect reverts until block.timestamp exceeds that future time; the bug stores the past _unlockTime and allows an immediate Collect, making the reference's revert requirement fail.

After any call to Put, the unlockTime of the caller must equal the max of the passed _unlockTime and the current block.timestamp; the buggy version leaves unlockTime unchanged from its prior value, so a later Put with a higher _unlockTime will not update it.

After any sequence of calls to Put, the caller's Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime must equal the maximum of all _unlockTime arguments passed in those calls and the block.timestamps at the time of those calls; the buggy version leaves unlockTime at its initial zero value (or a prior unchanged value) because it never assigns it, causing future Collect calls to succeed earlier than intended according to the supplied unlock times.

After a Put call, the caller's unlockTime must be at least block.timestamp and equal to the passed _unlockTime if _unlockTime > block.timestamp; the buggy Put never updates unlockTime, so a later Put cannot raise an earlier-set unlockTime.

After calling Put with a non-zero _unlockTime strictly greater than the current block.timestamp, the caller's unlockTime must be at least _unlockTime; the buggy version never assigns unlockTime, so it remains zero, allowing premature Collect.

After a call to Put, the LogFile contract's History array length must strictly increase in the original contract, but the mutant fails to add a new message so the length remains unchanged.
For any successful call to Put, the HistoryLength of the Log referenced by C must be strictly greater than it was before the call; the buggy version omits the log call so the length stays the same.

After depositing via Put, a user's unlockTime is set in the future; the reference C must revert or not update balance on Collect before that time, while the mutant allows early collection, resulting in different acc.balance for msg.sender after the call.
